items.title: Karl Berger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014
items.q: Even Albert Ayler didn’t think that way.

ctx.x: And you said the relationship of rhythm and playing with a rhythm in free jazz sometimes is controversial. Like was it, you said in Berlin if you were playing free jazz you weren’t supposed to be playing steady time?

Yeah. There are factions of free jazz movements, particularly actually in Europe and not so much here, that insisted that time was sort of out of the question, like you would not go there. And that’s still the case. There’s a few free jazz festivals in Europe where you cannot play time, like they would like pull you. And in America nobody quite thinks like that. Even Albert Ayler didn’t think that way. You know, like they just think of movement and you can play that in time, out of time, but there has to be that…
phenomenon by the way. I mean The Beatles wrote songs and they followed the words. Like there are some words that just fall on five and then the beat is there. Which is the blues too you know.
